Baby Cheesecakes

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Makes 12 mini cheesecakesPrep 25 minCook 20 min

These delightful individual cheesecakes offer a sweet and comforting note to the Childermas Banquet, a gathering often held after the solemn observance of the Feast of the Holy Innocents. Their small size and delicate flavor are a gentle nod to the innocence remembered on this day, providing a moment of shared warmth and reflection among family and friends.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (150g) graham cracker crumbs
  • 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
  • 1/4 cup (56g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 2 (8-ounce/227g) packages cream cheese, softened
  • 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • Fresh berries or fruit compote, for serving (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
  2. In a medium bowl, combine the graham cracker crumbs and 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar. Pour in the melted butter and mix until well combined and the crumbs are moistened.
  3. Divide the crumb mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups, pressing it firmly into the bottom of each liner to form the crust.
  4. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the softened cream cheese until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes.
  5. Gradually add the 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar to the cream cheese, beating until just combined and smooth.
  6. Beat in the egg, vanilla extract, and salt until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
  7. Spoon the cream cheese filling evenly over the crusts in the muffin tin, filling each cup about two-thirds full.
  8. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the edges are set and the centers are just slightly jiggly.
  9. Remove from the oven and let cool completely in the muffin tin on a wire rack.
  10. Once cooled, transfer the cheesecakes to the refrigerator and chill for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, before serving.
  11. Serve chilled, optionally topped with fresh berries or a small dollop of fruit compote.

Tips

  • Ensure all cold ingredients, especially the cream cheese and egg, are at room temperature for a smooth, lump-free filling.
  • Do not overmix the cream cheese filling once the egg is added; overmixing can introduce too much air, causing the cheesecakes to crack.
  • These mini cheesecakes can be made a day in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
